Process lesson: a research subagent reported RunPod H100 at $2.89-$3.29 and implied the skill's $1.99-$2.69 was stale. The live pricing page shows Community Cloud at $1.99 / $2.59 / $2.69, so the figure already in the skill was correct and applying the reported correction would have introduced an error. Only Lambda's range had actually moved. Verify every reported price against the provider page before changing it.

Process lesson on evidence sourcing: a live FX quote page is unusable as a citation because its number changes on every fetch (2.9772, 2.9766, 2.9763 within one hour), so any pinned snippet fails the next source check. The dated Bank of Israel SDMX observation is stable and re-checkable forever, and is marked verified_via api because the endpoint is CSV with no prose to quote. Prefer dated observations over live tickers for anything that goes into evidence.json.

Structural change worth keeping: all volatile pricing and credit figures now live in references/pricing-and-credits.md (and the Hebrew mirror) with a single 'read on 19 August 2026' stamp at the top. That file is designed to be re-verified and replaced as a unit each cycle, rather than hunting figures scattered through the body. Next cycle, start there.

Expert CRITICAL fixed: Step 2 asserted 'Data transfer out is the same pricing globally'. It is not, and the error was baked into evidence.json (which recorded the eu-west-1 rate as if it were global), which is why the gate passed it for cycles. Measured from the AWS Price List API: il-central-1 internet egress is $0.110/GB for the first 10 TB against $0.090 in Ireland and Virginia, and inter-region egress OUT of Tel Aviv is $0.08/GB against $0.02 out of Ireland, asymmetric against inbound. Egress is the category this skill exists to get right and it was the one category declared a non-differentiator.

Expert CRITICAL fixed: the commitment section was discount percentages with no obligations, while Example 2 recommended 3-year reservations to a company mid-migration. Now carries a per-provider table of cancellability, what the commitment is denominated in, scope, and escape hatches, including the 1 February 2027 Azure exchange cutoff, which falls inside the horizon of any 3-year decision taken today.

Expert CRITICAL partially addressed: the VAT rule was stated as 'exclude VAT for B2B with a valid tax invoice'. The reviewer's proposed mechanism (Israeli-branch billing means B2B is charged and then deducts input tax) is directionally right, but the AWS Israel tax page would not render for me and I did not confirm it at source. The skill now explains the ex-VAT versus inc-VAT distinction and the deduction mechanism, tells the reader to verify the billing entity per provider, and routes non-straightforward deduction positions to an accountant, rather than asserting a mechanism I could not verify. Confirm the AWS/Azure/GCP/Oracle Israeli billing entities next cycle.

Expert MAJOR fixed and it inverted a headline number: the il-central-1 compute premium was stated as 5-15%. Measured across ALL 324 shared Linux instance types via the AWS Price List API it is a flat 5.0% median (range 4.3-5.9%), invariant across families. An agent taking the 5-15% midpoint doubled it. The corrected picture is that compute is a small flat premium while network is 22% and 4x, which is the opposite of what the skill previously conveyed.

Judge finding fixed: four figures that evidence.json itself had flagged for a content fix had never been applied to the body, in either language. AWS Savings Plans (~66% vs the published 72%), Azure Reservations (a 40%/65% split Microsoft does not publish, against 'up to 72%'), and the me-west1 GA date and 'first Middle East region' claim, which were unevidenced and are now dropped. Lesson: when an evidence entry records 'this needs a content fix', that is a work item, not a note.

Judge finding fixed: the Hebrew file still shipped a GCP spot anchor ($0.073/hr) that evidence.json had already marked stale, because the English file dropped it in an earlier pass and the Hebrew was not touched. Any figure removed from one language must be removed from the other in the same commit.

Judge finding fixed: Kamatera was described as having five Israeli data centres including Petah Tikva and Haifa. Its pricing page lists exactly one Israeli location, Tel Aviv. Unverified footprint claims are as decision-changing in a residency discussion as unverified prices.

Process lesson: extracting volatile detail into references/ to satisfy the word cap is easy to get wrong. One extraction in this cycle silently truncated the entire Reference Links section off the end of SKILL.md because the slice took s[:i] + replacement with no tail. Caught by the heading-parity check, not by the word count. After any block move, re-run the parity check and diff the heading list, not just the validator.
